news.title: Ben Shapiro says 'whiff of corruption' surrounds the president he campaigned for
news.og_title: Ben Shapiro says 'whiff of corruption' surrounds the president he campaigned for : NPR's Newsmakers
news.og_desc: Conservative host Ben Shapiro says he is holding to his conservative values in the unstable era of President Trump.The host of The Ben Shapiro Show voted against Trump in 2016 but also campaigned for him in 2024. He’s disappointed in the president’s tariffs, alleged corruption and the execution of the Iran war.“I regret the way the president has performed,” Shapiro tells host Steve Inskeep in this episode of Newsmakers. “I don't regret my vote. I don't have a time machine.”Shapiro says Trump’s aggressive immigration enforcement and the general “whiff of corruption” that surrounds the White House — specifically the Trump family’s crypto company World Liberty Financial — all contributed to the Republican Party’s midterm losses in Congress, governor's mansions and state legislatures.He believes that Republicans have an “uphill road in 2028” and that Vice President Vance isn’t the ideal Republican presidential candidate. He argues that Vance would shrink Trump’s winning 2024 voting bloc of Hispanics, the working class, women and college-educated individuals.Shapiro points to Secretary of State Marco Rubio as a potential 2028 Republican candidate with broader appeal and a larger coalition. But he says many within the current White House will likely be damaged by association.Shapiro also unpacks his new movie, Confession — featuring Rob Lowe and James Franco — and the recent decline in his show’s YouTube subscriptions.Newsmakers is where you'll find NPR's biggest interviews. We post new episodes as soon as they're available — any day of the week. Follow or subscribe on Spotify, YouTube or wherever you watch or listen to podcasts to get new episodes as soon as possible. You can also find Newsmakers on the NPR app.Newsmakers relies on supporters who value independent journalism and a free press.     استقبل صاحب السمو الملكي الأمير محمد بن سلمان بن عبدالعزيز آل سعود ولي العهد رئيس مجلس الوزراء، في الرياض اليوم، قائد القيادة المركزية بالجيش الأمريكي الأدميرال براد كوبر والوفد المرافق له.
    وجرى خلال الاستقبال استعراض أوجه العلاقات الثنائية بين البلدين خاصة في المجالات العسكرية، بالإضافة إلى بحث تطورات الأوضاع الإقليمية.
